div.head: ECf 34.1a
div.ab:
Et hoc etiam precati sunt eum pro anima regis Eadwardi, qui sibi concesserat regnum, et cuius erant leges, nec aliorum exterorum. Tan
dem consilio et precatu baronum adquieuit. Et sic auctorizate sunt leges regis Eadwardi. [Ad Do Wo Ck No Ed 1: auctoritate leges sunt confirmate in Eo qui uiuit et regnat per infinita seculorum secula. Amen!]
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 661–662 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.
Liebermann’s numbering of the notes in the ECf column starts again at 1 on p. 662: the notes 1–5 to the part of this clause on p. 662 are distinct from the notes 1 and 29–32 on p. 661.

After “Et sic” Liebermann prints the rest of the sentence in two columns side by side: on the left “auctorizate sunt leges regis Eadwardi”, and on the right, headed “Ad Do Wo Ck No Ed 1”, the ending of those manuscripts. The right-hand column is given here in square brackets after the left-hand one.
The note on the London collection’s interpolation (*) is printed across the whole page; it is given with both columns.

Barone, um 1070 wesentlich Normannen, bitten ihren Normannischen Herrn um Angelsächsisches Recht!
barons, around 1070 essentially Normans, ask their Norman lord for Anglo-Saxon law!

Thomas uero archiepiscopus§ et Mauricius episcopus scripserunt propriis manibus omnia ista predicta per preceptum predicti regis Willelmi interpolirt Lond. — §) Cantuariensis fügt zu Ld [fehlerhaft]; die beiden Namen beginnen die Zeugenliste einer Urkunde Wilhelms I., die in der Gildhalle copirt war (Lib. custum. 28); daher wohl bringt sie der Londoner hier anachronistisch: Thomas von York sass 1070—1100, Morix von London 1086—1107. Diess verschlimmert der Lichfielder o. S. 627*

Lond interpolates Thomas uero archiepiscopus§ et Mauricius episcopus scripserunt propriis manibus omnia ista predicta per preceptum predicti regis Willelmi. — §) Ld adds Cantuariensis [wrongly]; the two names begin the witness list of a charter of William I which had been copied in the Guildhall (Lib. custum. 28); that is probably why the Londoner brings them in here, anachronistically: Thomas of York sat 1070–1100, Maurice of London 1086–1107. The Lichfield man makes this worse, above p. 627*
suorum fügt zu Ad Do Wo
enden Ad Do. Explicit fügt zu Wo; Finitur (finito em.) libro, reddatur gratia Christo fügt zu No
Ad Do end here. Wo adds Explicit; No adds Finitur (finito emended) libro, reddatur gratia Christo
